title: How To Actually Build A $10K/Month Business (15 Lessons)
summary: A serial entrepreneur's 15 lessons: start with no money, go full-time, own equity, give equity to staff, sell outcomes not hours, look after existing customers, and treat stock investing as a scam.

assertions.quote: having no money at all is actually a competitive Advantage because you've got nothing to lose

verdicts.note: Overfunded startups do waste capital, but undercapitalisation is among the top causes of small-business failure; the examples are survivorship-selected.

Family income is a powerful predictor of becoming an incorporated entrepreneur: a $100,000 higher 1979 family income is associated with an almost 60% higher probability of incorporation after controlling for ability, traits and education, which the authors read as credit constraints materially hindering entrepreneurship; the paper tests entry rather than founder discipline, but points the opposite way to the claim.

In a large representative panel of Norwegian start-ups, founders in the 30-95 wealth percentiles earn 8 points higher return on assets than the poorest 30 percent, while the richest 5 percent earn 2 points less (raw returns 11, 18 and 8 percent); the authors read the top-end drop as a less alert or dedicated management, so abundant wealth may hurt, but having little money is a disadvantage against moderately funded founders rather than an advantage.

assertions.quote: if you don't pay you don't pay attention is a lie pedal by people selling courses

verdicts.note: Course completion rates are very low regardless of price, which undercuts the pay-to-pay-attention line used to sell coaching.

assertions.quote: ideas are actually worthless only those that have had one idea think it has any value

verdicts.note: Investor and founder consensus holds that execution dominates, though some ideas have genuine defensible value and NDAs matter in specific technical contexts.

assertions.quote: you cannot build a company part-time
I've made all my money from when I've sold my businesses and I owned equity in the businesses that I sold

verdicts.note: Incorporated business owners earn 48% more residual hourly (28% at the median) than comparable salaried workers, but the median unincorporated owner earns less per hour than his salaried counterpart and unincorporated owners outnumber incorporated ones; owning a business pays only for a select group, and the paper measures hourly earnings, not wealth.

assertions.quote: A good rule in life in business is the faster you rise the quicker you fall

verdicts.note: Rapid growth without systems does correlate with collapse, but many durable companies also grew fast; the rule is a heuristic, not a law.

BLS establishment survival shows the closure hazard falls with age: of the March 1994 cohort 79.6% survived year one, about 90% of year-4 survivors made it through the next year, and 94-96% of survivors older than ten years survive each further year, so durability accrues over many years; the table says nothing about businesses that rise fast.

assertions.quote: I don't buy stocks and shares I think they're a scam I can't control their outcome

verdicts.note: Diversified index investing has delivered positive real returns over every long period on record; lack of control is not fraud.

assertions.quote: you only need three customers to build a business

verdicts.note: Retention is cheaper than acquisition and referrals compound, but a three-customer business is fragile to losing any one of them.

assertions.quote: 10 of them failed and they failed because they did it on my own the 19 that succeeded I had a co-founder

verdicts.note: Startup studies find mixed results: co-founded companies raise more and grow faster, but solo founders have comparable survival in some datasets.
